sentences.text: The Regional Flow Platform enters the winter operating mode when freezing precipitation, contamination reports, or low surface temperature forecasts make untreated ground movement unreliable.
The Meteorology Briefing Officer confirms the trigger conditions in the Digital Briefing Room so that airport, airline, and tower participants share one operational assumption.
In this mode, the Capacity Assessment Module reduces practical departure capacity to account for deicing time, pad transit time, and slower ramp taxi speeds.
The Airport Capacity Plan is revised with a winter margin before the Slot Allocation Engine recalculates affected Calculated Takeoff Time values.
The Deicing Coordinator maintains the active pad configuration, including open bays, closed bays, fluid limitations, and vehicle availability.
Pad queue controls assign aircraft to a deicing lane only after the Target Off Block Time is stable enough to support a realistic treatment sequence.
The Ramp Movement Board displays each aircraft as pending push, taxi to pad, in treatment, awaiting release, or returning to stand when treatment cannot be completed.
Ramp Control Lead uses the queue card to verify pad entry order before authorizing a movement from the staging area.
When demand exceeds the safe holding capacity near the pad, the Departure Metering Service withholds further push clearances until the pad queue falls below the configured threshold.
The Tower Sequence Manager reserves departure sequence positions only for aircraft with an achievable pad release time and a valid runway taxi path.
The Airport CDM Portal records the selected fluid type, mixture ratio, treatment start time, treatment completion time, and expected holdover reference for each treated aircraft.
Fluid status updates are timestamped through the Time Synchronization Service so that ramp, tower, and airline users interpret treatment age consistently.
The Ground Handling Dispatcher updates remaining fluid inventory and truck serviceability when replenishment, contamination, or equipment faults affect the planned treatment rate.
The Handling Resource Planner compares fluid inventory with scheduled deicing demand and warns when a planned bank cannot be supported without resequencing.
The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews aircraft readiness and may request a later pad entry when crew, catering, or passenger status would cause holdover time to be wasted.
Gate Conflict Detector produces the Gate Reopening Memo when a stand becomes usable after snow clearance and the gate occupancy constraint has been removed.
Quartzline must coordinate every pad release with the Tower Supervisor before the aircraft leaves the treated area.
Under freezing conditions, the Tower Supervisor protects runway departure spacing by accounting for reduced braking action, slower lineup, and possible repeat treatment requests.
The Surface Surveillance Adapter confirms that aircraft leaving the pad follow the assigned route and do not block inbound traffic to the same treatment complex.
If a treated aircraft cannot depart within its applicable holdover reference, the Deicing Coordinator marks the treatment as expired and returns the aircraft to the appropriate queue state.
The Common Situation Display highlights expired treatments, pad closures, fluid shortages, and ramp blockages so that participants can resolve conflicts without separate status calls.
The Collaborative Decision Log captures winter-mode decisions, including capacity changes, pad flow restrictions, and agreed deviations from the normal departure order.

When conditions improve, the Regional Flow Manager authorizes a controlled transition from Capacity Reduction State toward Recovery Phase after pad backlog, runway condition, and surface flow indicators are stable.
The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares planned treatment throughput, actual pad occupancy, and departure compliance to improve winter capacity assumptions for future events.
